mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of the trade/commercial register of any foreign corporate shareholder (proof of existence and authority of signatories)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade registry in the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; no consular legalization where both countries are Hague Apostille Convention parties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports / national identity cards of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority or a notary in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for certifications executed by a notarial or public authority; otherwise consular legalization if the non-EU country is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized domestic service-of-process / registered office consent from the Luxembourg registered-office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary, or donor if the consent is executed inside Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed outside Luxembourg in an Apostille state; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of any non-French, non-German, or non-Luxembourgish supporting document (e.g., corporate bylaws, powers of attorney)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the translator's signature alone is sufficient; no apostille for documents issued within the EU legal zone

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the U.S. OFAC SDN List, and (iv) the Luxembourg domestic FIU watchlists and RCS blacklists. Enhanced due diligence is mandated by the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, for any politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, or known close associates of PEPs. Screening must be documented, risk-tiered, and repeated whenever new sanctions are issued or ownership changes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any language using the Latin alphabet; however, the legal form suffix must appear as 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' (or 'S.à r.l.'). Where the intended name is not in French, German, Luxembourgish, or English, a certified transliteration into Latin characters is required before the RCS will accept the reservation. The articles of association must be drafted in or translated into French, German, or Luxembourgish, and the notarial deed must be in one of these official languages.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the RCS, the applicant may submit a corrected or alternative name reservation within the existing 30-day window, or file a formal administrative appeal to the President of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in commercial matters within 15 calendar days of the rejection. In parallel, the notary may address a reasoned request to the Minister of Justice for preliminary authorization if the rejection is solely based on a sensitive token that is accompanied by a planned statutory license or official approval. The administrative appeal procedure is set out in Article 32 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS, and, where the rejected token implicates a regulated activity, the authorization must be obtained from the competent minister before the appeal will be entertained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office consisting solely of a postal or correspondence address is generally not permissible for an SARL that will conduct physical parcel consolidation, because Luxembourg company law requires a genuine 'siege social' situated in Luxembourg and a physical location where the management can be contacted and records are kept. A co-working suite or serviced office with a physical address, a lease, and local management presence is acceptable if such presence is not merely sham or mailbox-only. Given that ISIC 5229 (freight transport agency and parcel consolidation) does not require a regulated license, the practical tolerance for a low-cost physical office is moderate; however, the tax authorities and commercial registry may challenge insufficient substance if the company cannot demonstrate a real, permanent establishment in Luxembourg.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated; Title V, Articles 710-1 to 710-20 concerning the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and company and annual accounts filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), operated under the Ministry of Justice via the eJustice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) together with the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically through eJustice/RCSL and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a SARL the minimum issued and paid-up capital is EUR 12,000. Cash contributions must be fully paid up before incorporation and deposited into a temporary blocked account with a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank must issue a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) that is released only after RCSL registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, the articles of association of the SARL dated [date], as executed before the notary, are approved in full and shall be filed as a parcel consolidation hub under ISIC 5229. RESOLVED, the subscribed capital of EUR 12,000, paid into the blocked account, is confirmed. RESOLVED, the registered office located at [address], Luxembourg, is adopted. RESOLVED, [Name] is appointed gérant, with sole authority to represent and bind the company, and [Name] is appointed compliance officer to support RCS, tax, social and licensing filings. RESOLVED, the gérant is authorized to open bank and payment accounts, engage domiciliation agents, and obtain industrial, fire safety, environmental and occupational permits required for the hub. RESOLVED, all prior lawful acts of the incorporators are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Corporate Name and Verify Name Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL name-reservation service via eJustice.public.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the RCSL database for identical or confusingly similar names; submit the application for a negative certificate/name reservation using the proposed registered name; include the corporate object in ISIC 5229 to allow accurate designation. The reservation is valid for three months.
required_dossiers: Short description of corporate purpose (cross-border parcel sorting and direct-injection linehaul)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL raises a similarity objection, revise the name with a distinctive element and refile; an express refusal may be appealed to the administrative tribunal within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Association and Capital Plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary for authentic incorporation deed; domiciliation agent for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French or bilingual form, including legal form SARL, corporate purpose, registered office in Luxembourg, share capital of EUR 12,000, share classes, transfer restrictions, manager appointment and fiscal year. Incorporate the capital escrow requirement and a Luxembourg domiciliation agreement; pre-agree with the notary on the deed execution schedule.
required_dossiers: Completed domiciliation agreement or lease of registered office in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary returns a revision memo; amend the articles and reintroduce the revised text. Any unresolved corporate-object comment may be handled with narrowed objective wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Capital Account in Luxembourg and Obtain Blocking Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation; inject at least EUR 12,000 in cash; request a bank certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming payment and irrevocable blocking until RCSL registration; ensure funds are released only upon registration or return to subscribers if the application fails.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide certified source-of-wealth evidence; request a renewed blocking certificate if registration occurs after the original certificate's validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Notarial Deed and File Registration with RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL Registration Department, Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Luxembourg notary, sign the deed of incorporation and articles; the notary files the application for inclusion in the RCS via eJustice together with certified attachments and payment of registration duty; monitor the RCS draft number until final registration.
required_dossiers: Capital blocking certificate from Luxembourg bank
Manager(s) consent and criminal record extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCSL queries lack of signature or documentation, the notary files a sworn rectification statement; substantive contradictions in the articles can be cured by a notarial rectifying deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS Extract, RESA Publication and Tax/Social Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations; retrieve the RCS extract with the Luxembourg national corporate number; file VAT, corporate income tax and net wealth tax registration forms via MyGuichet/ACD; register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale as employer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD does not issue a VAT number automatically, submit a written request with a certified RCS extract and statuts; any lapse in social registration must be remedied by back-dated employer registration with an explanation letter to the CCSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Operating Bank Accounts and Payment-Provider Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and third-party payment providers, including Airwallex and Local Clearing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, present the final RCS extract and RESA notice to the chosen bank; configure local clearing and Airwallex payment rails for direct-injection linehaul collections; appoint AML authorized signatories and complete corporate banking forms.
required_dossiers: AML compliance policy where transaction volumes are material
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's due diligence delays onboarding, supply a concise business plan and expected parcel volumes; request a written additional-information list; use a licensed EMI partner pending corporate bank account opening if permitted by the corporate treasury policy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, Craft and Commerce (Direction Générale de l'Industrie, de l'Artisanat et du Commerce)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (commercial establishment licence) under the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions, issued for the parcel consolidation hub and linehaul logistics activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency) of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B/Class 2 registration and screening; a full EIA report is not required below the Annex thresholds under Luxembourg's EIA law of 15 May 2018. A full EIA may be required for large logistics installations, floor areas over 15,000 m², or projects in sensitive environmental zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal wastewater discharge permits and Luxembourg water protection law; no untreated process water may be discharged to surface water or sewers. Vehicle emissions meet Euro VI standards with idling-reduction controls. Packaging waste must be recovered in accordance with EU Directive 94/62/EC and the national waste management law. VOC and combustion emissions remain below the limit values of the Luxembourg Grand-Ducal regulations implementing Directive 2010/75/EU (IED).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps clearance for fire load, evacuation routes, extinguishing systems and hazardous material storage; structural engineer's load certificate for racking and mezzanine floors; workplace inspection by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines covering occupational safety, forklift traffic plans, noise, manual handling, first-aid equipment and worker welfare facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – direct tax authority; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – VAT/registration; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) – customs; secure e-filing portal: MyGuichet (https://guichet.public.lu/en)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SARL before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through an authenticated notarial deed; the RCS automatically transmits the company's incorporation data to the AEDT for VAT number (numéro d'identification à la TVA) issuance. Simultaneously apply for a corporate tax reference number (numéro de référence) with the ACD. A foreign company that is not resident in Luxembourg but has a permanent establishment or supplies taxable operations in Luxembourg must apply for a VAT ID through form 640C/12 (TVA registration application) filed via MyGuichet, attaching the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, proof of place of business, identity of legal representatives and an EORI number where customs transactions are planned.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' classification election exists under Luxembourg tax law. However, an election is possible under Article 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LITL) to form a tax consolidation group for resident companies. A VAT group election is available under Article 62 of the VAT Law, enabling qualifying entities established in Luxembourg to be treated as one taxable person. The Luxembourg IP Box constitutes an elective patent box regime in respect of qualifying IP income. The ATAD-consistent hybrid mismatch rules (Law of 18 December 2017) apply automatically without any elective mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 net annual turnover for small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 aggregate intra-Community distance sales threshold for non-resident suppliers; mandatory registration where a fixed establishment or Luxembourg place of business exists (no de minimis).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime currently applies. B2B e-invoicing is valid when generated in a standard European format (EN16931) with the buyer's consent. VAT returns, recapitulative statements (Recap) and annual listings must be submitted electronically through the MyGuichet e-filing portal. Reporting thresholds and formats align with EU VAT Directive. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) project is expected to impose uniform digital e-invoicing from 2028, but not yet law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported to destinations outside the EU may be zero-rated (0%) provided the exporter (1) retains evidence of export within 90 days of delivery, (2) holds a valid export declaration accepted by customs, and (3) maintains transport documentation proving departure from EU territory. Freight forwarding and ancillary services (sorting, consolidation, packing, handling, temporary storage) connected with internationally moved goods may benefit from a 0% rate, provided they are directly supplied to the international carrier/consignor or linked to a documented export operation. Intra-EU supplies require the counterpart's active VAT number and evidence of shipment to another Member State.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A / SAD) validated by the Administration des douanes et accises (ADA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note showing physical movement from Luxembourg to non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement (SWIFT/SEPA) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in EUR within the statutory window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg AEDT may challenge zero-rated export treatment if documentary evidence is incomplete or contradicted by shipping records. Standard audit limitation period is six years from the due date of the VAT return (ten years in cases of suspicion of fraud or tax evasion). Late assessments attract interest at the legal rate (currently 4.5% p.a.) and penalties for recalcitrant taxpayers can escalate to 100% of the tax due. Criminal penalties for false VAT declarations include imprisonment and/or financial sanctions where fraudulent export schemes are detected. Retroactive cancellation of zero-rating will result in VAT, interest and penalties being collected from the taxpayer, and possible liability of directors under corporate law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) acting as the competent national authority for banking licensing, AML/CFT supervision, and compliance enforcement under Luxembourg law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is a fully convertible currency within the Economic and Monetary Union. Luxembourg maintains no unilateral exchange-control restrictions on current-account or capital-account operations. Capital movements and current payments are liberalised under Articles 63–66 TFEU, subject only to EU sanctions, AML/CFT (notably Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers) and statistical reporting obligations to the BCL. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is not subject to an exchange-control permit or conversion approval; the practical hurdles are corporate-law distribution tests, economic-substance expectations, and Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% domestic rate, reduced under tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive). There are no restrictions on holding foreign currency accounts in Luxembourg or on repatriating export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no time limit for converting or retaining export receipts. A Luxembourg SARL may lawfully keep foreign-currency receivables in its bank accounts, convert at negotiated commercial rates, or use them for trade settlements without BCL approval. Credit institutions may collect balance-of-payments and monetary statistics for the BCL/ECB, and all cross-border payments must satisfy the EU Travel Rule, but no percentage of export proceeds must be repatriated or converted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account / SEPA Settlement Account
Operational Account / Treasury Settlement / Commercial Trade Finance Account
Operational Account / FX and Payments Account / Capital Escrow Account
Settlement Account / SWIFT Clearing / Letter of Credit Facilitation Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EU/EEA-licensed e-money institutions and payment institutions that are passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 and supervised by their home-state regulator, provided they maintain client-money safeguarding and full Transfer of Funds Regulation compliance. An example is an Airwallex-type EU-licensed EMI operating through virtual IBANs and SEPA clearing rails; this is feasible for operational FX, local collections, and high-frequency parcel-settlement payments. However, an EMI is not a Luxembourg credit institution and does not offer the same deposit-guarantee protection; the legal constraint is that it cannot take deposits or engage in commercial banking lending without a CSSF credit-institution licence. Non-EEA offshore digital banks are rated Low unless they obtain a Luxembourg/EU passport, because they lack direct access to SEPA/TARGET2 and may present AML substance concerns.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not require all directors to appear physically if a compliant CDD process is followed; remote video identification and electronic signatures are permissible under the amended law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance. In practice, most tier-one Luxembourg banks require at least one managing director or beneficial owner to complete a physical or secure video interview before account activation, and they typically require apostilled corporate documents, passport copies, proof of address, and a certified copy of the SARL articles and notarial deed. For non-resident directors or complex group structures, a physical interview at a Luxembourg branch or a corresponding European branch is frequently imposed. Remote opening is possible for a low-risk parcel-consolidation SARL, but the bank may impose an initial 1–3 month transaction restriction and enhanced source-of-funds verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered non-EEA ownership structure above the LU SARL, with nominee shareholders or fiduciary arrangements masking the ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart, Luxembourg and foreign company registry extracts, share register, notarised articles of association, UBO declaration signed by each relevant director, source of wealth documentation for UBOs holding 25% or more, tax residence certificates, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border e-commerce parcel-settlement flows that appear to mimic an unlicensed payment aggregator or client-funds pass-through.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written logistics master agreements proving that the SARL is a principal consolidator rather than a payment intermediary, segregated treasury accounts for own-account funds only, sample invoices with parcel manifests and customs declarations, flow diagrams showing that no third-party client funds are collected, a tailored AML/CFT procedure, and a statement confirming freedom from payment-institution licensing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-sensitive payment corridors or high-risk jurisdictions indicated by seller, consignee, or marketplace patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/OECD sanctions screening policy and logs, restricted-country list embedded in the commercial contract, transaction-level counterparty KYC for the ten largest logistics customers, evidence of effective destination/consignor controls, HS-code-level customs documentation, and periodic CRF/sanctions screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency for the Luxembourg SARL, such as no physical office, no local employee, and foreign-controlled management with an otherwise low-risk business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease for Luxembourg premises, payroll and social-security filings for a Luxembourg-resident manager, board minute records held in Luxembourg, CSSF-compliant bookkeeping and accounting records, registration with the Luxembourg beneficial-ownership register, VAT identification, and a credible business plan covering the parcel consolidation hub.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds disparity between the initial capital injection and the projected turnover of a cross-border e-commerce parcel hub.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the contributing shareholder, notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase resolution, escrow agreement, loan documentation if applicable, cash-flow forecast, evidence of existing logistics contracts, and independent audit or accountant confirmation of transaction forecasts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be made by bank transfer only, never by cash. For euro-denominated receipts from EEA shareholders, use SEPA Credit Transfer to the LU SARL IBAN. For non-EEA transfers, use SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 with cover instructions for high-value transfers), including the recipient legal name, LU IBAN, BIC of the receiving bank, and a purpose wording such as 'Capital contribution to LU SARL' or 'Shareholder loan to LU_SARL'. The receiving Luxembourg bank must be provided with the notarial incorporation deed or capital-increase resolution, share register, UBO declarations, source-of-funds bank statements, and commercial justification before final credit. No BCL exchange-control approval is required, but the bank will verify that the sender and beneficiary are not on sanctions lists and that the transfer complies with the EU Travel Rule requiring full remitter and beneficiary data. Any in-kind contribution must be separately documented and reported in the corporate filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the primary rails are SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated invoices within the EEA, SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA disbursements, and TARGET2 for irrevocable euro settlement of high-value logistics payments through the participating Luxembourg bank. For large parcel linehaul, freight, or customs-duty cascades, commercial documentary letters of credit under ICC UCP600 and standby letters of credit may be used with the bank’s trade-finance desk. For high-frequency low-value disbursements to consolidators, an XML pain.001 file may be submitted to an EMI or local clearing provider, but full SWIFT/SEPA traceability and transfer information compliance must be preserved. All outbound payments should be reconciled against ISIC 5229 business documents such as parcel manifests, consolidation invoices, customs declarations, and warehouse dispatch records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other fully convertible currencies, documented under an ISDA 1998 FX master agreement or a local bank master agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on narrower-convertibility Asian currencies, such as cash-settled CNY/USD or CNY/EUR trades, provided the counterparty is a MiFID-licensed institution and the transaction is characterised as commercial hedging against parcel-supply-chain payment exposure
EUR and foreign-currency options, collars, and zero-cost risk-reversal structures for protection against adverse exchange-rate moves on cross-border logistics receivables
FX swaps and swap-driven spot rollovers for short-term liquidity management and settlement funding between the SARL’s operating currencies
Cross-currency swaps (XCY) for long-term intercompany shareholder loans or acquisition-related treasury exposure, subject to EMIR clearing and margin rules and MiFID II suitability requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with management report and auditor's report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; calendar-year SARL due by July 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder, criminal fine up to EUR 5,000, joint and several director liability; persistent non-filing triggers court-convened winding-up and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS declaration (déclaration annuelle) confirming registered office, managers, shareholders and activity data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year; window January 1 to December 31 aligned with anniversary of RCS registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Presumed inaccuracy of RCS data; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; repeated failure forces LBR referral to the Public Prosecutor and may lead to judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax (IRC) and municipal business tax (ICC) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by December 31 following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; e-filing season opens March 1.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; ex officio assessment with up to 10% surcharge; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) and confirmation of minimum net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed jointly with the CIT return; December 31 following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex officio tax assessment, monthly 0.6% interest, enforceable seizure of corporate assets; minimum net wealth tax applies even in loss years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic VAT returns (monthly or quarterly) and annual VAT recapitulative adjustment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly returns by the 12th day of the following month; quarterly returns by the 15th day following the quarter; annual recapitulative data included with the final period return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-return administrative fines, interest on overdue VAT, AEDT best-knowledge reassessment, and criminal penalties in case of fraudulent omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CRS / FATCA annual report of financial account information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via the OECD-compliant electronic gateway
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 following the calendar year of the reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 250,000 under the amended CRS law; late or incomplete reports may additionally trigger foreign exchange penalties and audit scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, final deadline December 31; share-transfer-triggered updates must be filed within 30 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 per infraction; repeated failure can suspend dividend distributions, trigger register restrictions, and expose managers to criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting (assemblée générale annuelle) and ratification of accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; minutes kept in the statutory minute book (no RCS filing unless articles are amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end; calendar-year SARL by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court convocation at shareholder request; managers jointly and severally liable for losses caused by failure; non-approval of accounts does not cure late-filing penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GLEIF-accredited Local Operating Unit (LOU) serving Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the LEI certification expiration date, typically aligned with the registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: LEI becomes lapsed, blocking securities settlement, bank KYC processing and certain regulatory filings; reinstatement fees apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000, net turnover EUR 8,800,000, average 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for financial-sector undertakings, public-interest-related structures, or upon request of shareholders holding at least 10% of equity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and accounting (implementing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be applied voluntarily; accounts presented in EUR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must confirm the accuracy of its RBE beneficial-ownership data once per calendar year, due by December 31. Any share transfer changing the UBO requires a mandatory RBE update within 30 days of the transaction so the UBO register mirrors the share register. Confirmation is performed electronically through the LBR/RBE portal; failure triggers fines up to EUR 5,000 and restricts corporate distributions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 - 5,400 per year (EUR 1,500 - 5,000) for Luxembourg registered office / domiciliation agent and company secretarial support; add approximately USD 88 for LEI renewal.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,600 - 27,000 (EUR 8,000 - 25,000) for a mid-market independent certified audit when mandatory; nil for small SARL qualifying for the audit exemption.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined corporate income tax rate (17% IRC + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption for net qualifying IP income; participation exemption for dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings; investment tax credit; notional interest deduction (3% on new equity); SOPARFI regime can reduce effective tax close to 0% on qualifying holding income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1002 (Déclaration d'Impôt sur le Revenu des Collectivités), filed electronically via eCDF / MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on 30 June following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension of one month if filed electronically; additional extensions available upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, registered seat, local Luxembourg tax number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SARL's official name, address in Luxembourg, and the local tax identification number (LVN). Do not list foreign addresses as the principal seat.
Provide the RCS number of the Luxembourg SARL; if foreign-controlled, ensure the RCS registration is up-to-date with current managing directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit or loss for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income as a Luxembourg tax resident. For any foreign PE, attach separate annex to claim DTA exemption/credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total amount of corporate income tax due after prepayments and withheld taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only fill in if foreign parent withholding or local prepayments exist; attach proof of prepayments. If no French/German border commuter matters, leave blank.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 0.5% per month on assessed tax, min EUR 10 and max 10%; late payment interest 0.6% per month; administrative fine up to EUR 1,000; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 for intentional non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (qualifying 10% holding for 12 months); treaty rates typically 5%–15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain an official tax residence certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; (2) submit a withholding tax reduction request to the Luxembourg paying agent before distribution using the relevant form; (3) if excess WHT was withheld, file a refund claim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) within the statutory period (generally by 31 March of the following year).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: no statutory Luxembourg withholding tax. Royalties: no domestic withholding tax; Luxembourg treats them as business income and may tax via a Luxembourg PE. Under treaties, royalty WHT is usually 0%–10%, but domestic exemption already applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 per year; Master File required for MNE groups with consolidated turnover >= EUR 750,000,000; CbC Report above same threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No Cayman/BVI-type ESR regime, but Luxembourg enforces economic substance through GAAR, EU ATAD Principal Purpose Test, and domestic substance-based anti-abuse rules. A SARL must have real local substance (registered office, physical presence, employees, meetings) to obtain tax residence, treaty benefits, and participation exemptions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false statements or intentionally omitting taxable income, or using artificial constructions to shift profits from the consolidation hub to zero-tax shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of tax, monthly late interest (0.6%), fines ranging from 10% to 200% of underpaid tax; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if gross negligence or fraudulent misrepresentation is proven; imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and maintain TP documentation by the filing date, or materially distorting remuneration to non-arm's length pricing in cross-border parcel consolidation transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to reflect arm's length profit, late payment interest, and penalty of up to 10% of adjustment; secondary adjustments may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who directly set non-arm's length prices may be personally liable for penalty assessments and interest; travel bans and asset seizures may be imposed during enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Denial of Substance Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LU SARL without Luxembourg office, employees, or economic decision-making, solely to obtain treaty benefits or the EU Parent-Subsidiary 0% dividend rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, rejection of the participation exemption, re-qualification of dividends subject to 15% WHT, and potential assessment of additional taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors may owe civil damages for facilitating sham structures and may be prohibited from acting as directors for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments or parcels for sanctioned persons/entities, or intentionally blinding the company to criminal proceeds using the e-commerce parcel hub for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000; confiscation of assets; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil liability for laundering losses, travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification under Luxembourg company law.
